reviews.text: Creed III is emotionally and viscerally satisfying.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: Creed III is one of the biggest highlights of the Rocky/Creed franchise to date, and Michael B. Jordan proves that he can handle himself in the director’s chair
reviews.author: Branyan Towe

reviews.text: Boxing might be the most cinematic sport, and this might be the best boxing has ever looked.
reviews.author: Joshua Polanski

reviews.text: As the film builds to it's emotional and physically demanding climax, Jordan pulls out all the stops for an at-times visually inspired smackdown.
reviews.author: Paul Klein

reviews.text: A dizzying, vicious dance peppered with slo-mo close-ups and visceral sound effects that make a case for why this might be the best boxing movie since Sylvester Stallone’s original outing.
reviews.author: Jessica Toomer

reviews.text: The film takes some risks for a sports movie and although not all of them have a perfect landing, the cast and Dreamville Records executive production bring an electrifying soundtrack that makes everything right.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Peterson

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan’s film is a stirring tale of brothers who turn against each other out of hurt and love
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: The third and best chapter so far focuses on Donnie wanting to retire a champ and blend his business and boxing talents to create Adonis Creed Athletics.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: The heart of this championship series is still there but it is just a step slower.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: But because Creed III plays things as straight as it does and is as "well-behaved" as it always is, what happens instead is that those cheesy training montages end up feeling like obligations rather than joyous celebrations.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: Everyone may have an underdog story, but “Creed 3” reminds its audience that while we may be through with the past, the past is not through with us.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Creed 3 is a KNOCKOUT! The most emotional, ferocious, personal Creed film yet. The best fight choreography in the entire franchise! Completely anime inspired
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Creed III is not a complete knockout, but certain moments are. There are gut punches and there are swings and misses. Above all, though, Creed III is an exciting directorial debut for Jordan and a pure, powerhouse showcase for Majors.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: "With his eye toward healing, Jordan’s directorial debut is a fantastic technical and emotional achievement in the “Creed” canon and a triumph of the restorative power of Black male softness."
reviews.author: Brooke Obie

reviews.text: Creed III can go toe-to-toe with the heaviest hitters of boxing cinema.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: This is a film series where the characters feel like a warm blanket. It is pleasing to revisit them, and see how their lives have changed and grown.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: Unfortunately he didn’t spend enough time on character development, and the audience is stuck with one-dimensional character that don’t have a redeeming bone in their bodies, which is a shame for a franchise that earned it’s love by opening its heart.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: More than the first two Creed flicks, this one breaks away from the tried-and-true formula.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Without the presence of Sylvester Stallone, in front of or behind the camera, and without Rocky Balboa in the film, Creed III still manages to tell a Rocky story in which boxing is a metaphor for struggle, and a champ can still become an underdog.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Creed is told to be happy with what he's got. And it's pretty good advice, given how he's recently retired, relatively healthy, and has plenty of money and a loving family. Yet he still allows a handful of playground taunts to bring him back to the ring.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Creed III comes alive as a result of Jonathan Majors and Michael B. Jordan's emotionally charged performances.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: Creed III’s success serves as inspiration in more ways than one. A lot of Black talent was behind this film, from production and execution to promotion, it’s been a busy week for Michael B. Jordan.
reviews.author: Lina Lecaro

reviews.text: When the film's antagonist plays his scheme close to his chest the film achieves an effective level of drama. When all is revealed the film seems desperate to overdrive itself so it can catch up to its inevitable confrontation in the ring.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: The increasingly sophisticated fight choreography, as rendered via the bloody ballet between Majors and Jordan, is the bread and butter of the genre.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: In one amazing sequence, the crowd at a big fight goes missing, being replaced by a post-apocalyptic ghost land with only the two fighters’ grunts supplying the sound. The camera often whips around the fight as a big exchange is unfolding.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Creed has to definitely become Apollo and survive this transformation in which his ex-friend is much more like Rocky. Thus, destroying the past and rebuilding from it seems to be something that closes not only Creed's arc, but also Rocky's.
reviews.author: Agustín Acevedo Kanopa

reviews.text: A spectacle as vibrant as usual and drenched in the trademark Balboa spirit —with an extra dose of sugar, though—.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: “Creed III” feels like a summation of sorts, but also a new beginning — because it shows a franchise, and a character, finally walking out of the long shadow of Rocky Balboa.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Nothing really motivates us... Adonis, maybe it’s time to really hang up the gloves!
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: There’s a line late in Creed III that sums up this installment perfectly — “The Creed dynasty reigns supreme.” That’s appropriate for a franchise that keeps knocking out one sequel after another without taking a bad outing to the chin yet.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: It checks all the boxes to keep people who want all their sports competition film needs met (hello training montages!) with enough to satisfy the dramatic storytelling needs of someone who can’t tell a Balboa from a Drago.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: By delivering the expected and doing so with style and intensity, it lands in the top tier of the nine Rocky universe movies, although falling short by a few titles from the pinnacle.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Better than the second Creed, worst than the first, and that's pretty much the best-case scenario it was worth hoping for.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: After nearly 40 years, this franchise is still punching.  This time around they prove the series can work without Rocky or Stallone.  The real standout here is Jonathan Majors who plays one of the best antagonists in the series.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: Jordan makes a few unnecessary forays into expressionism to make this point, but he needn’t have. The climactic bout has more than enough impact without getting into the ring with Scorsese.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: It’s one of the best films of the year...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: It's so predictable that you knew what was going to happen within the first few minutes. But this movie did hit the feels, particularly with the storyline with Adonis' daughter and Damian.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: It's a bit too predictable but very entertaining with strong direction by MBJ. Jonathan Majors is almost too good as he was on another level...wish there were more scenes between him and Tessa Thompson!
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: You can replicate the character dynamics of the original series & its story beats – you can chuck in an exhilarating montage, and direct the climatic showdown with style. But without the heart that powered the original movies, it’s a mechanical pastiche.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: A first-rate outing, which shows great potential on Jordan’s part as a director
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan’s directorial debut Creed III escapes the shadow of Apollo, Rocky, and Drago and finds new ground for Donnie and the Creed spin-off series to build their own legacy.
reviews.author: Paul Risker

reviews.text: Creed III is a thoroughly surprising movie. There is an attention to detail and symbolism that quite frankly has no business being as well done as it was.
reviews.author: Frantz Jerome

reviews.text: Despite the well-worn path this story travels, it is very well acted and directed. As usual in this series, the fight scenes are expertly staged, but it isn't all about blood, violence, anger and hatred. It is also about love, friendship and respect.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Creed III is too sleek, too rushed, and too contrived to deliver [all] the emotional payoffs it promises.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: While “Creed III” has that nagging feeling of unfinished business, it also doesn’t have the skills of Sylvester Stallone’s Rocky. Rocky, in fact, isn’t even a fond memory in this outing.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: The visuals are full of action and energy.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: Solid installment!... Pretty pedestrian, but goes places I really like.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: Creed III is no knockout it's still a worthy bout.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: MBJ proves to be equally equipped to provide strength and brilliance both inside the ring and outside of it, stepping into Coogler's massive shoes with great competence. Jonathan Majors is a STAR.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: Every time a new franchise offering comes out, I'm doubtful we need it, yet, so far they've all been notable and proven that the blade is still sharp, and this new offering isn't an exception. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: It's a powerhouse film whose hardest blows take place outside the ring.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Creed III is a winner, with Jordan and Majors bringing their epic talent to the boxing ring.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: It packs a punch but it seems like you have been ringside at this fight in the past.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Proving that the Rocky saga doesn’t necessarily need Rocky himself, Creed III continues to build and improve on what came before, whilst also showing it can stand alone as a fine movie in its own right.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Creed III is promoted as a boxing movie, but is really a tale of pain, regret and the power of brotherhood.
reviews.author: D. Watkins

reviews.text: Worth the price of a ringside seat.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: An uneven but often powerful threequel...
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Creed III has largely succeeded in stepping out of Rocky’s shadow, and Adonis looks more than ready to go a few more rounds before hanging up the gloves for good. Just like his predecessor, Adonis isn’t going down without a fight.
reviews.author: Miles Surrey

reviews.text: While Creed III features a well-drawn, menacing adversary in Jonathan Majors’s Dame Anderson, it doesn’t utilize him enough.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Creed III is much more sure-footed in presenting a fascinating emotional struggle for its title character as well as a physical one, even if it ends up diminishing its most subversive plot threads.
reviews.author: Kambole Campbell

reviews.text: There are a couple of decisions that take place in the film in terms of story that get a little hokey... [but] by the time you get to the finally fight, Michael B. Jordan does something really interesting with the fight sequences.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: For a first-time director, Jordan does a very good job, notably in the film's handful of fight scenes, understanding the ballet of the match.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: Creed III occupies its own world. Maybe that's sufficient. I'd give Creed III a pass but I wouldn’t be sorry if Jordan were to hang up the gloves and devote his considerable talents to other endeavors.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Jordan understands the difference between the emotionally direct and the simplistic, with his and Major’s lead performances bringing complexity to what could otherwise have been two-dimensional caricatures.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: There are some flourishes here (in Michael B. Jordan's direction) that's truly great. That final match at the end is one of the best action sequences in the entire franchise.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Creed III makes sure that the drama outside the ring is equally intense and gratifying. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: A great directorial debut by Michael B. Jordan, with an amazing/fierce turn by Jonathan Majors - one of the best opponents in the franchise's history. Great intense story for Adonis, with some elements of past Rocky films. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: I’m a big boxing fan and director Jordan delivers. He also gives Jonathan Majors a startling, overwhelming presence. Majors is the reason to see CREED lll. The fight scenes are amazing.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: ... While Creed III is entertaining it isn't at the stature of any of the previous entries. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: Majors is easily the best thing in this third Rocky offshoot...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: This is a respectable though predictable addition to the Rocky-Creed saga, but there is a moment that parents of kids may find cringy. This is star Michael B. Jordan's first outing as a feature film director and he does a solid job.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: Admirers of this boxing saga, adults craving drama, genre fans looking for a fight and those who enjoy excellent acting will go the rounds with Creed III. Why? Because Jordan doesn’t pull any punches. He lands them.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Jonathan Majors is compelling to watch in this film he plays the role [in a way that] says so many things without even saying a word.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: Creed III has its flaws, but it lights up whenever Majors enters the frame.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: We all love an underdog story, of course, yet commercial fiction doesn't have to be quite so divorced from hard fact. Still, if you can see past that... Creed III has its merits.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: If Zach Baylin and Keenan Coogler's script had been a little more gritty, or at least more subtle... Jordan's debut, asides from being an entertaining boxing movie, would have been memorable. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Rosado

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan does a great job in his directorial debut!
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: As a director, Jordan has a visual style that really works here. The story is told through extreme close ups that allow you to read every micro expression. Some points are hammered home, but it’s not like the Rocky films were ever known for being subtle.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: A heavyweight sequel from Michael B. Jordan.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Without surpassing the first "Creed", this new sequel is better than its immediate predecessor, and a great example of what Michael B. Jordan can do as director. Not bad considering it's the ninth (!) installment of the franchise. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Creed III lacks a convincing ending and above all, some kind of explanation on why Stallone is missing... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: After two films focusing on Adonis the fighter, this entry explores the man as a father, son, husband and brother. It’s the Rocky V of Creed films...
reviews.author: Joel Harley

reviews.text: Making his directorial debut, Jordan handles the action in and out of the ring with aplomb. The boxing matches are bloody and brutal, the frenetic camera zooming in on every painful body blow dished out by the pugilistic players.
reviews.author: David Michael Brown

reviews.text: Audiences will be impressed with Jordan's nuanced performance and Majors' humanized "heel" turn.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: Creed III captures the spectacle and ceremony of boxing, providing the audience with an entertaining thrill ride. It doesn’t reinvent the wheel, owing much to its predecessors in the Rocky and Creed series in story structure and character development.
reviews.author: Murtada Elfadl

reviews.text: ... the best surprise of the film is the development of Jordan as a director.
reviews.author: Colin Biggs

reviews.text: A hell of a calling card for its director, who flexes every muscle as both actor and filmmaker to construct a movie that, by excluding the Stallone-shaped elephant in the room, sees Creed break out on its own.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Strong acting and filmmaking almost make up for the way this sequel relentlessly celebrates toxic masculinity.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: No Stallone? No problem.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Despite some overwrought melodrama and questionable politics, Creed III succeeds as an emotionally powerful and visually exciting boxing movie.
reviews.author: Kyle Logan

reviews.text: While Rocky’s absence finally opens up some new avenues, the film fails to utilise these to their fullest potential. Jordan announces himself as a competent director, but perhaps it’s time for Creed to hang up the gloves for good.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: The obligatory training montage sizzles (complete with a joyful moment at the Hollywood Sign), while the fight scenes have a real stinging quality to match anything in the original Rocky films.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Creed III's climax is emotional, mythical and just plum superb filmmaking—a standout moment in an excellent film.
reviews.author: Justin Harrison

reviews.text: All of that being said, I wish this were the end of this series (I doubt it is), because I think it ends on a decent, satisfying note. Time and inspiration will tell.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: I'm sort of stunned by how much I didn't like this movie.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Stallone’s creation of Rocky in 1976 spliced New Hollywood grit with fairy tale appeal, letting it thrive in Star Wars’ blockbuster world. It proves malleable enough to go on without him, finding heroic character in more complex circumstances.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: Whatever the reasons were, it took something great and made it into something mediocre, an unfortunate end to this powerful trilogy.
reviews.author: TK Burton

reviews.text: There’s so much richness to the world depicted... so much available to dissect about Black masculinity, class distinctions, racial conflicts, capitalism, on and on, that it’s increasingly disappointing to see those aspects... get pushed aside.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: Here, the script is key, which carries all into a winning film, and I’d also say that Coogler has a future in directing—his creative shots and tightly framed scenes all added to the film’s impressive look.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: As a newcomer to directing Jordan does a decent job, though some viewers will question his decision to focus on drama rather than boxing. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The best thing is the chemistry between Adonis and Damian.
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Quite simply: it's a knockout.
reviews.author: Marriska Fernandes

reviews.text: Daringly, the film blurs the line between plucky underdog and snarling villain.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: It's enjoyable, yes, but it can't help but fall into commonplaces. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Roberto Landaverde

reviews.text: It's an engaging and strong entry into the series and even though you might be able to predict the end, it's worth the journey.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: The Creed movies (much like the Rocky films before it) tell stories rooted in the indomitable human spirit. Sure, they always end in a boxing ring with millions of people watching. But the undercurrent of humanity give the fights more weight.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: The movie has firmly established there is plenty of fight left in the franchise. On an even more important level, it establishes Michael B. Jordan as a talented director to follow.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Creed III doesn’t break major thematic ground, but it has powerful performances, charming family dynamics, and well-choreographed fights. Its aim isn’t huge, but it hits its thematic targets.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan's directorial debut is a mixed bag of high energy fight sequences and grounded drama, not quite living up to the exquisite storytelling level of the first two entries. This time, the whole isn't greater than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Patrick Hicks

reviews.text: More of a split decision than a knockout, CREED III immerses viewers in visceral boxing scenes but falls short in the character development that made the first two entries in this franchise such a delight.
reviews.author: Valerie Kalfrin

reviews.text: Take nothing away, Creed III is a knockout on emotion, heart and soul, ushering Michael B. Jordan as an exciting filmmaker to watch out for.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: My problem was that I never bought into this obvious fantasy boxing/character film, that tells us with a straight face it's better to be rich with no worries than poor with a lot of worries.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Not bad for Michael B. Jordan's freshman directing debut. The fight scenes are good. But if Stallone is out for good, it would seem the RU (Rocky Universe), quality-wise at least, is in danger of imploding.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Jordan is doing double duty here, directing as well as starring in this solidly by-numbers chapter in the ongoing Creed saga.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: It's a little heavy on montage, but since when has then been an issue?
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: Creed III packs a real punch with a truly gripping and emotional story and a scene stealing turn from the ever charismatic Jonathan Majors.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: Creed was an introduction of a new hero, Creed II was the hero becoming a champion and Creed III is the hero standing firm in his legacy.
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: If CREED III works – and it does – it’s not because it’s telling a story having anything to do with the world of professional fighting. It works because we can connect with the characters and what they’re going through outside the ring.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan makes a confident and selfless debut as an actor-director, sharing space in his ring with a heavyweight like Majors.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: While Sylvester Stallone sits this one out, it’s the 2023 secret weapon Jonathan Majors who gives the film its credence.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Creed III may be the first Rocky movie without an appearance from Sylvester Stallone but it proves that it’s fine to move on from the original icon. It didn’t need him.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: This round, it is Jordan in his directorial debut who offers dynamic visuals and ... still manages to keep us on the edge of our ringside seat.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Although it adheres to predictable formula, this crowd-pleasing installment provides a logical continuation from a narrative standpoint while taking the title character in a new direction.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: As a directorial debut for Michael B. Jordan, ‘CREED III’ is an audacious attempt and certainly projects his talents and prospects behind the camera.
reviews.author: Tony Asankomah

reviews.text:
I'm not going to use some trite expression, like "Creed III is a knockout!"
It is but I'm not going to say it like that. Instead, I'm going with the equally lame "Creed III is the undisputed champion of the world!!" It's a great movie.
reviews.author: Adam Olinger

reviews.text: It is, admittedly, exciting to watch. Not because it’s Rocky. But because it’s Rocky reborn.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: The movie stays true to the tone of its predecessors, while adding an appealing new antagonist.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: It has the crowd-pleasing moments, sure, but the unlikeability of the main character and the obvious absence of Rocky makes this a bit of a chore.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Creed III packs one hell of a punch.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The first Rocky came out in 1976 and showed no sign of being the kind of movie that would spawn eight follow-ups. But with the inventiveness of Creed III, an old franchise suddenly feels fresh.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Imprisoned by industry formula, Jordan cannot rise above its patronizing clichés.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Jordan immediately places the ethical dilemma on the audience, forcing us to connect with the men merely by spending time in their physical proximity. It’s hard to categorize Majors as a villain, as Jordan paints the character with so much empathy.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: It’s a better one for being about exactly the conflict you think it’s about. This is the chickens coming home to roost, as the saying goes.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: It's predictable. You know exactly what is going to happen but it's an entertaining film
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: This franchise continues to put out solid entertainment and most of what you come to Rocky/Creed films for is present and done well. Some stylistic choices are sure to be divisive and there's some story issues that arise as the 3rd act begins.
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: A solid enough successor to those two films, and Jordan, in his directorial debut, manages to keep things running smoothly.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan's directorial debut is a more compelling urban drama than a ROCKY or sports movie. The actor/director delivers a well-oiled machine, cranking out the scenes that propel the story forward without wasting time on trivial sequences.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: Creed III hits above its weight when compared to Ryan Coogler’s knockout original, but that doesn’t mean Jordan’s solid sequel can’t hold its own as an entertaining boxing matchup.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: The nuance of Adonis’ internal dialogue is elevated further by the stellar performances of Jordan’s talented ensemble cast.
reviews.author: Ineye Komonibo

reviews.text: From the moment Majors appears leaning against a car, the charisma factor goes into fifth gear.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: This is a by-the-numbers Creed movie, infused with intimacy and originality that makes the film stand out. You get what you would expect but it continually strives to slip the predictable as well.
reviews.author: Kevin Sampson

reviews.text: The punches pop, the franchise feels freer without Stallone’s shadow, and Majors masters melodrama yet again. Next time I see him, I better be encouraged to cheer for him, because I’m gonna do it anyway.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Like its stellar predecessors, Creed III finds substance, heart, and glory in the beating and bloodying.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: First-time director/star Michael B. Jordan smartly flips the script on the Rocky saga with this forceful if fanciful melodrama.
reviews.author: Michael Sragow

reviews.text: With a dynamic, talented cast, Creed III delivers nuanced performances that radiate emotional depth.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: This latest entry in the Creed franchise just continues to build on everything we were shown in the first two movies, adding another entertaining chapter to the story of this boxer.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Creed III’s greatest achievement is demonstrating that there’s more story to be told about Donny, who after two films had been looking pretty thoroughly explored as a character.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: “Creed III” is the kind of pulpy entertainment associated with lesser installments in the prolific boxing movie franchise.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Creed III is, in certain ways, just like The Wrath of Khan: Someone from the protagonist’s past comes back to create severe drama that causes a return to action, and they’re both the best of their series.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Jordan is responsible for the film’s trials as well as its triumphs. While he unapologetically embraces myriad cinematic cliches, he also stages scintillating boxing matches, which is not  easy when the audience knows full well who’s going to win.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: The two Final Fight combatants are fearsome and beautiful to behold, and Jordan does his best to get visually creative, but there’s more drama in the training montage — possibly because it’s the only place where his character feels vincible.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Majors reigns as the de facto champ of this movie with a gravitas and world-weariness...
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: How did Michael B. Jordan star in and direct Creed III? The film reimagines the original Rocky with a more deeply troulbed Rocky challenger.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Jordan has long since proven himself as an actor of terrific charisma, versatility, and humanity; with “Creed III,” he shows he’s just as captivating on the other side of the lens.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: The hurried storytelling is frustrating, but the terrific performances and strong character development make this sequel much better than expected.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Still, even with the steady supply of clichés and occasional leaps of logic, the dramatic scenes smoulder away nicely.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Following the same arc as the "Rocky" franchise, the 3rd outing finds Creed contented and ready to retire, but first he must deal with looming issues from his past & a friend whose desire masks malevolence. Audacious directing debut by Michael B. Jordan.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: The past is prologue in the Rocky Universe, and Jonathan Majors creates another worthy rival in Damian to Michael B. Jordan's Adonis. Despite the easy way Dame gets a shot at the title, the contrast in this one is between who made and who is left behind.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: "Creed III" seems to want to throw out what worked before, and go it alone. That's about the worst strategy a boxer can have.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: For his feature directing debut, 'Creed III' star Michael B. Jordan turns in a solid but exceedingly safe fight drama.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: One of the franchise's more grounded films.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The film is all about the brilliant performances of Michael B. Jordan and Jonathan Majors.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: 'Creed III' star and director Michael B. Jordan's complete understanding of his characters' inner and outer realities gives him the confidence needed to take rewarding risks in his directorial debut.
reviews.author: Francisca Tinoco

reviews.text: The biggest challenge for this third installment was to infuse it with Stallone's symbolic and creative weight. That's hard to pull off when you don't even have the balls to name him. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan delivers a knockout of a directorial debut.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Despite my own dislike for the final product that 'Creed III' is...the film delivers on the cinematic components that audiences not only crave, but demand now more than ever from a blockbuster film like this.
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: Creed III isn’t perfect, but it’s an entertaining movie with visceral fight scenes you won’t find in a superhero fantasy... It’s an unapologetically masculine film about imperfect men trying to figure out how to live in a world that’s passing them by.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: Obviously, the fisticuffs are the bread-and-butter of films like this, but the theme of fractured masculinity is where the real battle plays out, making “Creed III” a distinctive and somewhat daring entry in the franchise.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Star and first-time director Michael B. Jordan uses newfound free space to his advantage. Haymakers and uppercuts aren’t the only bold swings taken here. If Creed is the best of the Rocky films, Creed III works because it’s barely a Rocky film.
reviews.author: Conor O'Donnell

reviews.text: Creed III is not as successful as the first two films in the series, but it has more than its fair share of interesting moments and cinematic fights.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Creed 3 has the wrong protagonist. We should be rooting for Dame Anderson, not against him.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan returns as star and now director to play the boxing champ who comes out of retirement to take on a fierce new contender (a dynamite Jonathan Majors). Even when the overcrowded plot stumbles, this clash of the titans is worth cheering.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Even with a remarkable director/actor across the ring, it’s Majors that emerges as the film’s champion.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The reigning champion nepo-franchise.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: I'd call the movie a split decision. It falters occasionally but, in the end, "Creed III" wins.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: A film that, despite being underwritten at crucial points, is better than any third entry in a franchise has a right to be.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: Sadly all the elements that made the first two films so accessible and engaging are nowhere to be found here.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: It helps that Jordan has an actor of Majors' calibre at his disposal. The actor plays the role with an eternal shiftiness, the broad and yet false smiles, the resentment simmering beneath the grinning façade if one really cares to look.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: Majors dominates, prowling through each scene as if he were a sly, observationally carnivorous velociraptor craftily stalking its prey. I couldn’t take my eyes off him.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: While Creed III may not be a total knockout, the film lands enough punches to entertain audiences.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: With his unnervingly nonchalant gaze and jaw jutting forward, Majors radiates hidden, explosive danger, and his formidably brawny physique makes an understatement of Dame’s boast to have kept in shape in prison.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: “Creed III” should have some box office punch.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Admittedly, still relying on the tropes of most boxing movies, but officially paving its own path, guided by the superb direction of Michael B. Jordan, Creed III stands tall in the ring and packs an emotional punch.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: There are punches so visceral you’ll feel like you’re in the ring.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: With a rushed timeline and no real character growth, “Creed III” does nothing to differentiate itself as an entry in the broader series of both Rocky and Creed’s stories or in the boxing film subgenre.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Creed III is a fantastic sports drama and probably the best heavyweight fight we’re gonna see all year.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Jordan is also a bit too literal in his efforts to symbolise how these two men have been imprisoned by their pasts. But for the most part the fight sequences are distinctive enough from the previous films to at least feel fresh.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Like any good title fight, "Creed III" needs a rematch.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Creed III is a winning movie that delivers exceptional performances alongside standout fights in an impressively stylish manner.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: What Jordan does best as star, director and producer is showcase Majors’ heavyweight performance, cementing him as one of our brightest stars. Taking over a behind-the-scenes role is a part of the “Rocky” legacy, and Jordan takes the reins with ease
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Although there is nary a mention of Sylvester Stallone’s Rocky Balboa in this one, the indomitable spirit, grit and heart that made the 1976 original a surprise hit is still alive — 47 years later.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Jordan, as director, delivers a captivating blend of explosive energy and melodramatic intensity; he sharpens the stark lines of conflict with keen attention to performance... and a controlled, storm-like feeling of moods building to crises.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: As a director, Michael B. Jordan finds new ways to keep the boxing part of this boxing movie fresh and interesting.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: The Stallone-free debut from Michael B. Jordan bashes life into the boxing movie genre.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: In one corner, a nuanced psychological drama with modern ideas. In the other, a decades-old beast that falls back on clips of grown men punching trees and pulling biplanes on their shoulders.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: We probably didn’t need a third Creed film, but in his directorial debut, the franchise’s star Michael B. Jordan proves more than capable of hitting the right beats and telling a straightforward story without getting distracted by cinematic gimmicks.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Starring (and now directed by) Jordan, this is a stirring, conventionally entertaining boxing film that stands on its own two feet.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Creed III is one of the best entries in this long-in-the-chipped-tooth franchise. More interesting still, its success pivots on a fairly subversive idea: What if Rocky was the bad guy?
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: With Creed III, Jordan does go all out in proving he can give audiences a sufficient fight movie. But, just like all the Rocky pictures Stallone directed, it’s mostly a mighty, mediocre show.
reviews.author: Craig D. Lindsey

reviews.text: The original hero, unlikely heavyweight champion Rocky Balboa, is out of sight and barely referenced... As compensation, this leaves room to appreciate Creed III as a pretty good standalone boxing melodrama, at least for the first two thirds.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: A showcase of technical craft, script wizardry, thoughtful direction, and some of the best performances you’re apt to find anywhere, let alone in the ninth movie in a half-century old franchise.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Quality film that’s better than the bulk of Rocky movies.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: No movie franchise has lasted so long in such relative good health. Creed III certainly deserves to be seen. And it deserves to be seen on the biggest screen with the largest portions of the most unhealthy snacks.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: The friction between the two gives the film a real sense of grounded emotion and makes the climactic and inevitable final fight a rousing and refreshing respite from the typical formula.
reviews.author: Trace Sauveur

reviews.text: Bulking up the back story slows the pacing, in a movie that finally delivers the goods but whose broader ambitions under director/star Michael B. Jordan get boxed in by its ring-shaped formula.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Better than Creed II — and Jonathan Majors keeps the champ on his toes.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The boxing and training scenes have got a kineticism that jumps off the screen. And the performances from Jordan, Tessa Thompson as wife Bianca and -- especially -- Jonathan Majors as Damian, are all more than fine.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: “Creed III” stands on its own and Jordan proves that Adonis is still a character worth rooting for.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Creed III doesn’t hit the heights of the first movie in the series, but it proves that Michael B. Jordan can be a director. That and Majors’ performance are what I take away.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Puts every camera movement at the service of the story.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Santiago Alverú

reviews.text: The script throws out a couple of surprises that Jordan handles deftly and carefully as the film’s director. Creed III, however, is a boxing movie, and he handles that aspect effectively as well with well-choreographed action and building tension.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Creed III tells a story that takes the best parts of the Rocky franchise and blends them into a sort of rock-’em-sock-’em comfort food, so fighting-form slick it slides down your gullet like a raw-egg smoothie.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Jordan is his usual excellent self, also showing great competence behind the camera, but this is Majors’ film from the time he shows up.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Director/star Jordan hits hard; Screenplay still needs more punch.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Creed II frustrated me. I thought it'd be about the guy with everything & a big moment of self-awareness. But instead it makes excuses for success-fueled aggression, lack of perspective, & an inability to find the best way to make a right out of a wrong.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: Creed III is a film that looks good, has some fleeting moments but never quite lives up to the previous two films. It winds up being a disappointing entry in a franchise I’ve grown to expect more from.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Jordan keeps the film clear of head and light on its feet. As Creed III glides and grunts to its close, the series feels anything but spent.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Come for the boxing, yes — but bring plenty of hankies, too.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan seems more invested in making *his* movie than "a Rocky movie," which doesn't necessarily make 'Creed III' great, but it makes it better than it should be.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: The showdown between former friends turned rivals is a classic story we’ve seen before. Jordan still amps up the energy with classic Creed/Rocky training montages, the roaring crowd scenes, and the tender family moments between Donnie, Bianca, and Amara.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Its hokey and familiar quality comes off as formulaic...while the movie isn’t an embarrassment, it’s far from a knockout.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Like all the Creed films, III reimagines its Rocky forebears in better taste: empathy for “villains,” better roles for women, honest conversations between Black heroes and antiheroes.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: A well-crafted male soap opera that features thrilling boxing sequences and, yes, a sweaty, grunty, pre-showdown training montage.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: A sluggish story that telegraphs where it’s headed to the point that even the revelations feel inevitable.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Jordan is let down in a big way by cinematographer Kramer Morgenthau, who flattens all these evocative images into a hazy, low-contrast, digital blur.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: On one hand, Creed III is more of the same that audiences have come to expect from the Rocky spin-off series, but on the other, it’s a popcorn movie made with brains and heart.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: It’s the addition of Jonathan Majors (currently on screen giving Ant-Man and the Avengers a run for their money and who is having a moment) that punches up the stakes of a franchise that needed a fresh direction.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Some underfed elements keep the film from being a knockout, but this is still a franchise entry to be proud of.
reviews.author: Cheyenne Bunsie

reviews.text: Creed III distances itself from Rocky's shadow and the film is all the better for it.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Jordan's shot at directing himself is about as deep an emotional dive as the dual franchise has achieved. It touches everything from our own mortality to how we face the sins of our past. It would be nice if the series were to end as a tidy trilogy.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: After three movies, Adonis is still guarded and insecure, but literally fighting his past isn't a particularly compelling way for him to move forward.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Creed III isn’t really a sports movie. Blows are exchanged, and there’s even a lo-fi training montage but this is more about the trauma of the past revisited in the present, than the action in the ring.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Jordan’s directorial debut starts strong but tires out in the final round.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: …a sombre but perfunctory continuation of the Creed saga into the era of cannabis-flavour energy drinks…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: While Majors reminds audiences that 2023 is definitely his year, Michael B. Jordan not only delivers a solid, poignant and entertaining directorial debut but establishes himself as a promising filmmaker.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: The characters overcome the very predictable script.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: "Creed 3" punches up enough emotions and excitement to satisfy any "Rocky" fan. It's a crowd pleaser that will hit even harder while watching on the big screen.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: Creed III promises something different, so it's a shame it ends up being more of the same.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Probably the first Creed (or Rocky) movie that would have benefitted from a therapy montage, but Creed III still knows how to play the undying franchise's greatest hits.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: The sense that [Michael B.] Jordan owns this character is palpable, and his directorial prowess only enhances his stronghold on the character.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: The Creed series continues to be a more interesting examination of class, caste, and American meritocracy than the Rocky films ever were, all within the bounds of crunchy, buttery popcorn cinema.
reviews.author: Dylan Roth

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan and Jonathan Majors face off in a boxing story told with style, taste and respect for the audience.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: No Rocky, no problem.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: The formula is familiar and the plotline predictable in “Creed III,” but there is an authentic undercurrent between the heavyweight stars Michael B. Jordan and Jonathan Majors playing childhood friends turned professional rivals.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Giving the gloves to Michael B. Jordan both in front of and behind the camera leads to satisfying results, and the year of great Jonathan Majors performances continues.
reviews.author: Amon Warmann

reviews.text: watching [Creed III] is like wearing an old sweater – very familiar and a little comforting.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Creed III is a fascinating, thought provoking and electrifying film! Michael B. Jordan delivers as a director. Jonathan Majors is intimidating, captivating and empathetic as Damian. Is it a knockout? No. But you're gonna go thru some things for 12 rounds.
reviews.author: John Rocha

reviews.text: In the end, every theme finds a physical mirror in the ring: the drama of life writ large in left hooks. And nobody gets to retire from that.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: We are just two months into the year 2023, and already cinema has successfully imparted a message that will not soon fade from thought: Jonathan Majors is a phenomenal actor.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: A serviceable sequel, but can't land the knockout punch.
reviews.author: Michael Balderston

reviews.text: “Creed III” works as well as it needs to, and for the umpteenth film in a franchise, that’s more than enough.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The story that brings Majors and Jordan together is heartfelt, and genuine. However, it sacrifices the intense climax towards the end that made the first two films pop. Jordan should still be proud of his directorial debut, even with a few shortcomings.
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: When it comes to delivering genre thrills, Creed III really knows the ropes, powered by a pair of knockout performances that pack the kind of punch that'll leave you flat on the canvas
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Jordan makes his directorial debut with Creed III and shows some promise in that arena, but the screenplay by Keegan Coogler and Zach Baylin weighs him down.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: A solid, well-directed affair that does what all the best sequels have done thus far, which is to retell a variation on the basic Rocky story with all the attendant themes about self worth, fighting back, defying the odds and facing down your adversaries.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Jordan has taken the classic underdog story and flipped it on its head while giving Creed the heroic arc worthy of a trilogy.
reviews.author: Joey Morona

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan’s directorial debut is a well-acted, knockout threequel.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Creed 3 features some wonderful visual storytelling from first-time director Michael B Jordan. The story is familiar and not wholly original, but it still retains a compelling look at family, responsibility, and guilt.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: It’s not easy directing yourself acting in such a physical role about an iconic hero, and Michael B. Jordan does a mighty fine job doing both well. This film may not be a total knockout, but it delivers a solid punch.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: … isn’t a bad film, it just doesn’t quite live up to its potential.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: Even with some noticeable flaws, it’s hard not to get caught up in the story, the characters, and the themes beneath the surface. If only it had a few more knockout blows to make the film a rousing success like its predecessors.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: A promising debut for [Michael B. Jordan], who shows here that he’ll never let his own star ego get in the way of a film: Majors steals the show, and Jordan is there to capture it.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: As a directorial debut, it seems as though Michael B. Jordan felt the call and purposely stacked the deck against himself, only to still manage to go the distance.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Saddled as it is with a formulaic and forgettable script built on tropes, melodrama and tin-ear dialogue, when you get down to it, it’s just another mediocre sports drama.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Creed III has every ounce of emotion and action required to satisfy fans. Michael B. Jordan excels behind the camera, directing one of most expertly-crafted fight sequences ever. Jonathan Majors owns the screen-time he gets.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Fine but profoundly forgettable; easily the weakest of the three.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan and his cast and crew threaded the needle to create a crowd pleaser with both brains and heart.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Can this legacy sequel stand toe to toe with Balboa once Sylvester Stallone stepped away from the series? That question was answered with a first-round KO in Creed III – a film rich with unique and original fight sequences that are sure to spellbind fans.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: “Creed III” is definitely a people movie. And Jordan has trained his lens on the right subjects.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: A decade ago, another actor taking over and remixing the Rocky series would have seemed like pointless sacrilege. Now it seems like one of the few movie revival series with the drive to compete.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: "Creed III" is an intensely enjoyable continuation of the Creed story, one that doesn't pack a lot of surprises in its punch but nonetheless goes the distance.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: As of this moment, today, Jonathan Majors is a movie star.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: This sequel isn’t so much a knockout as a 12th-round split decision.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: It's a split decision on Creed III... [It's] a good first directorial effort by Michael B. Jordan, and definitely worth a shot with viewing, but it doesn’t go the distance.
reviews.author: Debbie Lynn Elias

reviews.text: Working from a story by original director Ryan Coogler (who, along with Sylvester Stallone, produces here), star Michael B. Jordan makes his directorial debut with a trilogy capper far more satisfying than the second film if less so than the first
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: A great standout for Jordan’s first film. The fights & choreography are some of the best of the trilogy, the relationship progression & character evolution that I really loved. Such great chemistry with the whole cast, yet Majors is a powerhouse here!
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: Creed III earns a place among the best boxing movies for expressing that the ring is more than a modern-day gladiatorial arena but, in cinema, a reflection of the interior lives of those inside it.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Creed III adds Michael B. Jordan's directorial prowess and a formidable new opponent in Jonathan Majors to the franchise.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: As both actor and director, Jordan pulls off some fancy footwork in Creed III.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: A triumph! Rousing, genuinely heartfelt and exhilarating. It will make you stand up and cheer!
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Another great entry in the Rocky / Creed franchise. Jordan proves to be a skilled director while Majors just keeps getting better and better. The boxing matches are also thrilling, although one creative choice doesn't quite work in the third act.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Creed III elevates a basic (but compelling) story with a very strong cast, while Michael B. Jordan's direction steals the show in a knockout film.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: In his directorial debut, Michael B. Jordan brings a surprisingly heartfelt though formulaic addition to the Rocky franchise.
reviews.author: Noëlle D. Lilley

reviews.text: The film carries on a long-running tradition of intermingling melodrama and pugilism with aplomb.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: This low-stakes outing is a letdown from first-time director Michael B. Jordan, who continues to star in the series.
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: I had myself a great time.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Whether Rocky fans will take issue with the lack of Stallone or some of the film’s bigger swings, there’s a confidence to respect in this film, as it tells a story which feels fresh within the established framework.
reviews.author: Liz Shannon Miller

reviews.text: It is, in my opinion, the best of the Creed franchise yet and a film that highlights Jordan’s abilities as both an actor and director. But this is also another star turn for Jonathan Majors.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: At its best, the movie takes the unlikely shape of a yuppie-in-peril thriller about chickens coming home to roost, Cape Fear reinvented into a Shakespearean sports drama.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Flirts with greatness, but pulls its punches one too many times.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: While Creed III is no match for the initial film that started it all, it’s still a smart, competent sequel that once again sees Adonis Creed forging his own legacy outside the shadow of his father and Rocky Balboa.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Every bit as relevant and distinctly Jordan’s, as the original Rocky was to Stallone.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: And while Creed III is certainly operatic in scale, it succeeds because it’s grounded in character dynamics.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: But just as a great boxer can’t pull the same trick over and over again, neither can a franchise, an issue previously the cause for the steep drop-off in quality among the nonetheless lucrative “Rocky” sequels.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: It’s easy to see the film’s punches coming before they’re thrown, but that doesn’t lessen their wallop when they land.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Creed III takes the literal and existential titles that once defined Apollo Creed and Rocky Balboa and gives them to Adonis as a way of signifying that this really is his story now and his alone to carry into the future.
reviews.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore

reviews.text: Overall, it's a fitting chapter. It's a bit stiff in places, and leaves the viewer asking for more emotionally between the 2 lead characters. The ending leaves the movie a bit cumbersome as well.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: A fascinating film from a new director who seems unafraid of moments of teary defeat that manifest into something far more introspective and self-nourishing — even when that’s between two brawny Black men at odds with each other and themselves.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: Creed III punches up, being the best-written, best-performed, and most dramatic entry yet. It’s big, it’s personal, and it’s strong.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: Jordan... makes some shrewd decisions – thematically, visually – that make Creed 3 thoroughly entertaining. No small feat, considering the potential pitfalls of diminishing returns.
reviews.author: Matt Maytum

reviews.text: Going back to its Rocky roots, this film is a drama first, and a boxing movie second.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: Creed III serves up more of the franchise’s winning combination of family drama, boxing fights, and friendship loyalty. The movie might disappoint viewers who are expecting more boxing scenes, but Adonis Creed’s complicated past gets a worthy spotlight.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: It may be a competent enough boxing movie, but it’s just another boxing movie, with absolutely nothing new to say or show.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan lands haymakers and heart in a predictable sequel that punches above its script. Creed III marks a solid feature directorial debut. An absolutely shredded Jonathan Majors brings depth, gravitas, and wicked jabs.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan remains fantastic as Adonis and understands how to stage decent fights, but as a first-time director lacks the finesse to tell and drive home drama believably
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Creed III comes down to a draw between its flashes of brilliance and its missed opportunities.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: Creed III offers a healthy mix of remixing franchise formula and charging its own path. It can be a tad blunt, but it has something worthwhile to say.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: 'Creed III' triumphantly shows how much the Black experience has to deal with survivors' guilt and how forgiveness given to each other for societal factors beyond their control is vital.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Creed III is another worthy entry to this storied boxing franchise and a strong directorial debut for leading man Michael B. Jordan, who is also in top form as Adonis Creed, but it’s ultimately Jonathan Majors that steals the show!
reviews.author: Rohan Patel

reviews.text: Isn’t as stirring as the previous chapters, but it sustains cinematic force and adds boxing intensity for Adonis, who apparently doesn’t have Rocky Balboa to rely on anymore.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Creed III is a knockout.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: As Sylvester Stallone did with Rocky Balboa, Michael B. Jordan made Adonis Creed a modern-day icon.
reviews.author: JimmyO

reviews.text: Morgenthau and Jordan make the creative decision to shoot Damian and Donnie’s climactic fight in a way unlike we’ve seen in the previous “Creed” films that amps up the story’s emotional stakes.
reviews.author: Meredith Loftus

reviews.text: Creed III marks a formidable bookend to the trilogy with no shortage of boxing extremity.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Creed III is a championship prize-fight worth watching with a crowd. Don’t be surprised if you find yourselves glued to the fisticuffs on-screen. From spectacle to heart, this movie delivers everything you’d want in a blockbuster sports movie.
reviews.author: Robert Butler III

reviews.text: Creed III does serve as a nice springboard to whatever future movies Jordan wants to direct. He’s done a really great job here. And it, of course, allows Jonathan Majors another chance to emote. Right now, Majors has to be the king of emoting.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Can the Rocky franchise exist without Rocky?... Creed III, finally, has actually answered the question at hand. And it’s done so with a firm and enthusiastic “yes”.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Majors simply is a sensation here, a sinewy strapped wagyu beefcake whose performance is layered with loss and anger and a depth of sadness that make what could have been a run-of-the-mill adversary into the real star of the show.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: An overcooked script... keeps Creed III from landing every punch it throws. Overall, though, it does prove victorious: Jordan clearly has directorial skill, and he and Majors make for a formidable onscreen duo.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: Creed III suffers from a certain lack of heft and specificity in its storytelling structure, a sense that the original bare-knuckle magic is not all there. But it's also often better than the blunt-force melodrama of the last film.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: A solid hit that could have been a gut punch, this chapter of the Apollo Creed story gets the job done.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: If Creed III turns out to be the last Creed movie, it will prove to be a satisfying finale. But if not, it keeps the bar high.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Creed III is a thrilling crowning of a new hero grappling with his own complicated legacy.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: An engrossing new visual dynamic to the fight scenes and a fantastic antagonist in Jonathan Majors’ Dame Anderson elevate it in the legacy of a franchise that’s no stranger to middling sequels.
reviews.author: Clint Gage

reviews.text: A rare sequel that comes close to restoring one’s faith in the worth and legitimacy of the franchise as a concept, the latest chapter in what might well be the best we have right now.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: Jordan uses the full power of IMAX to direct some glorious fight scenes... These flourishes will surely delight many fans of the franchise, even as the narrative -- the reason we keep watching Adonis fight in and out of the ring -- lets us down.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

reviews.text: Packs a powerful punch of emotion and heart as it teaches those watching how to forgive themselves for the mistakes they made in their lives. The cinematography, sound editing,  music, performances -- all come together to make something truly special.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: CREED III may not be a knockout boxing movie like its two predecessors, but it still lands plenty of dramatic power punches outside of the ring. If this is the end of Adonis Creed’s story, it's a fulfilling one.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: There are narrative road bumps involved in trying to reconcile the franchise’s American sports-drama roots with sports-anime inspirations, but the emotions hold it together.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Much like Adonis Creed himself, the film soars when it is paving its own path forward as opposed to resting on the laurels of the franchise's legacy, emphasizing heart and vulnerability over boxing brutality.
reviews.author: Patrick Cavanaugh

reviews.text: This film’s ability to introduce new characters, recontextualize old ones, and even play with new genres is satisfying and electric.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: While Creed III is checking boxes with the training montage, the family drama, and the uplifting ending, it’s a formula that remains as inspiring as it was when Rocky Balboa took on Apollo Creed in 1976.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: Creed III's visual language, as literal as it may be, offers up a beautifully rich film and a love letter to Shonen rivals.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Though Baylin & Coogler’s script gives just enough to not be forgettable, Jordan’s direction seals the deal and provides fulfilling entertainment.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: A predictable but solid sequel.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Creed III is a knockout film that delivers on every corner of the ring, and Michael B. Jordan’s directorial debut is triumphant.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: A B+ sports movie saved by some A+ movie stars.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: With Creed III, Jordan is learning from what has been done before and bringing this series into an entirely new generation, evolving this world in a way that makes it feel entirely new again.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: Smartly, rather than give audiences what they expect out of a third "Creed" film (Clubber Lang redux), "Creed III" goes smaller and more intimate without pulling a single punch.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan is competent behind the camera and the boxing scenes remain a highlight of the trilogy with the addition of Jonathan Majors as a welcomed newcomer, but the story struggles as the film finds itself on the ropes with little room to move.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: Rather than re-assembling and relying on more family trees, Creed III finds a very penetrating and personal singular focus for its choice of ominous opposition.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

synopsis: After dominating the boxing world, Adonis Creed (Michael B. Jordan) has been thriving in both his career and family life. When a childhood friend and former boxing prodigy, Damian (Jonathan Majors), resurfaces after serving a long sentence in prison, he is eager to prove that he deserves his shot in the ring. The face off between former friends is more than just a fight. To settle the score, Adonis must put his future on the line to battle Damian -- a fighter who has nothing to lose.
